questions: Should the function fill NaN values only in numeric columns (as in the reference solution) or in all columns (attempting to compute mean on non-numeric columns would raise an error)?
If a column is entirely NaN, its mean is NaN; should the function leave those NaN values unchanged, fill with something else (like 0), or raise an error?
Should the function handle CSV files that contain a header row? The prompt doesn't specify, but pandas.read_csv defaults to inferring headers.
Should the mean be computed excluding NaN values (pandas default) or including them?
If the CSV file exists but is malformed (e.g., inconsistent columns), should the function raise an exception or attempt to load it?
Should the function fill NaN values in place (modifying the original DataFrame) or return a new DataFrame?
Should the function handle datetime or timedelta columns? Their mean is defined in pandas, but the prompt only mentions numeric columns implicitly.
Should the function read the CSV with any specific encoding (e.g., utf-8) or let pandas auto-detect?
